head: e26733e3eab2e39c5fe6766fea8081bc54d30200
reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5 (independent reviewer for the F21 delivery session)
scope: The F21 diff against main at e26733e3e: the RUNBOOK overcompiled row and the README overcompiled line, read beside _commands, pf_runs, _names, _held_to and compiles in score.py, with probes of pf_runs and _held_to for options with no entry, refused entries and options, informational calls, the bare guide run and unsplittable segments. Excluded observation: the README's Run checks intro splits commands at ;, &&, || and | while _commands also splits at a lone & and a newline; scope evidence: the intro sentence is unchanged on main at 4b0466803 and the change touches only the class line; arising issue https://github.com/m2ux/prosiform/issues/805.
criteria: AC1: each pf call the overcompiled check counts is stated in both files. AC2: make check passes.
validation: Probes of pf_runs and _held_to under the unit checkout's venv.

findings.description: The RUNBOOK row gave the unsplittable-command case no miss condition.
The RUNBOOK defect condition sent a stated invalid call to the tables, which cannot state one.
The README exempted every informational call, while the scorer counts one the compiler refuses, as pf --help --bogus.
The README row named the malformed call otherwise than its Run checks intro.
The README row's sentence left unclear what 'or a sub-agent did' attached to.
'Words but no entry' was looser than the scorer's test of options with no entry.

head: 154fff13c04528a8abaac48e091b42d992eb94e0
reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5 (independent reviewer for the F21 delivery session, folded #804 and #805)
scope: The change aebc17ade..154fff13c folding #804 and #805, within the full diff against main: pf_runs' pick reading against Compile.tags and _picked, _commands' per-segment split flag, heredoc bodies, an unreadable first token, |&, a lone &, paths ending /pf, a pick beside other presets, the score.py docstring, the README Run checks section and overcompiled line, and the RUNBOOK overcompiled row. Out of scope, unchanged on main at 4b0466803: pf a.md # note scores invalid since comments are not removed, and (pf a.md) and command substitutions are not read as runs. Rejected observation, held for the user: a run beside a redirect a separator cuts short, as in ls > ; pf a.md, counts as made though bash runs nothing of a line holding a syntax error; the user's #805 rule counts an unsplit segment only when its first word names pf, and the shell's whole-line syntax errors are a wider design.
criteria: AC1, AC4 and AC5 met in substance; AC2 failed on ruff E501 at 154fff13c; AC3 test_score.py 248 passed.
validation: test_score.py 248 passed; probes of pf_runs and compiles under the unit checkout's venv.

findings.description: The rewrapped score.py docstring line exceeded the 88-character limit, so ruff check failed.
pf_runs tested the pick by truthiness while Compile.tags tests it for None, so an empty pick read as the listing.
test_an_unterminated_heredoc_invalidates_its_segment held a case showing a heredoc body as data rather than an invalidated segment.
No test held a malformed non-pf segment in the same command string as a pf run.
The RUNBOOK overcompiled defect conditions omitted a pf call whose heredoc runs to the end of the input, which the shell runs with a warning.

head: fb06ad50f38a9e61647212519e6d0304b4848dee
reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5 (independent reviewer for the F21 delivery session, folded #804 and #805)
scope: The change 154fff13c..fb06ad50f and the six findings it fixes. Rejected observation, held for the user: in pf a.md; ls >, bash parses the line and runs nothing, while the scorer counts pf a.md as made. That is the rule the user decided for #805, under which a segment that does not split whole counts only when its readable first word names pf; modelling the shell's whole-line syntax errors is a wider design the delivery holds as a question rather than applies. A partial fix stopping the reading at a redirect a separator cuts short was applied and withdrawn, leaving no break, docstring clause or test behind.
criteria: AC1 and AC5: the RUNBOOK row, README line, README Run checks and score.py docstring match _commands, pf_runs and _held_to. AC2: make check exits 0. AC3: make eval-harness exits 0. AC4: test_a_malformed_command_running_no_pf_passes_the_run_checks passes.
validation: make check exits 0 at fb06ad50f; make eval-harness 858 passed; test_score.py 249 passed; ruff clean.
